verdict.rationale: Zulip's first-party docs describe a topic model in which each conversation in a channel gets its own space, and community users repeatedly praise its threading, including creating threads 'on the fly from existing messages'. However, the docs frame this as starting a new topic rather than replying to a specific message, so keeping side discussions attached to the original message is only supported by community claims. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of replying from a specific message into a thread, and evidence that the thread stays linked to that original message.

support.subject: As a team-admin, I can reply in threads so side discussions stay attached to the original message

citations.quote: Lots of conversations can happen in the same channel at the same time, each in its own topic. You never have to worry about interrupting — each conversation has its own space.
In Zulip you can create threads on the fly from existing messages
The most important feature of Zulip is threading.
